actions.q: Do parents pay taxes on UTMA?
actions.target: Are UTMA and UGMA accounts taxed differently?

fact_basis.fact: Parents can elect to report a child's income on their own return on Form 8814 if the child was under 19 (under 24 if full-time student), had only interest and dividends (incl. capital gain distributions), had gross income under $13,500 (2025), and is required to file; the child then does not file a return
fact_basis.source: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8814.pdf (2025 Instructions for Form 8814, Purpose of Form)

fact_basis.fact: Under the election the first $1,350 is not taxed and the next $1,350 (to $2,700) is taxed at 10%; with qualified dividends/capital gain distributions it can cost up to $135 more than a separate return
A separate Form 8814 is needed per child; election made by attaching to the parent's timely filed return
Page text: 2025 kiddie tax tiers $1,350 / next $1,350 / above $2,700 at parents' rate
fact_basis.source: this page, FAQ "Are UTMA and UGMA accounts taxed differently?"
